strapline: A dry season ahead and 1.25 million in its path; two readings of freedom at 62; a police plan for Mandevu — and Red Arrows make history in Durban

stories.title: ‘Preserve this year’s stocks’: 1.25 million Zambians face hunger in the lean season as the Government activates its El Niño plan — but the Vice-President says the lights stay on
stories.excerpt: Two ministerial statements to Parliament on Friday 23 October set out what the 2026/27 El Niño season could mean. Vice-President Mutale Nalumango said about 1.25 million people in 93 districts could face acute food insecurity between August 2026 and March 2027 and that K31.7 million has already gone to the Disaster Risk Management Division; Green Economy Minister Gilbert Siame listed the ten driest districts and announced a US$3.6 million grant for weather stations. Asked about electricity, Nalumango said there would be no load-shedding.

image.label: The 2026/27 season
image.caption: The Government has activated a national preparedness plan for an El Niño season forecast to bring late, below-normal rains to the south and west.

body: Friday's business in the National Assembly was dominated by the weather. In two ministerial statements on Friday 23 October, Vice-President Mutale Nalumango and the Minister of Green Economy and Environment, Dr Gilbert Siame, told MPs what the Government expects from the 2026/27 rainy season and what it has done so far to prepare. Zambia Monitor, the Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers all reported from the House.

According to Zambia Monitor's account of the Vice-President's statement, the Government has activated a coordinated national preparedness plan in response to early warnings of below-normal rainfall, prolonged dry spells and possible drought. The scale of the risk comes from the 2026 Zambia Vulnerability and Needs Assessment Report: about 1.25 million people, or 7 per cent of the population analysed, could face acute food insecurity between August 2026 and March 2027, spread across 93 districts. Nalumango said K31.7 million has already been disbursed through the Disaster Risk Management Division to prioritised districts in nine provinces — Eastern, Southern, Western, Central, Northern, North-Western, Muchinga, Lusaka and Luapula — and that provincial authorities, rather than Lusaka, bought and distributed the relief food to save on transport costs.

body.text: I urge all Honourable Members to encourage their constituents to preserve this year's stocks
body.attribution: Vice-President Mutale Nalumango, ministerial statement to the National Assembly, Friday 23 October, as reported by Zambia Monitor

body.text: Where the rain is least likely to fall

body: Dr Siame's statement, reported by Zambia Monitor and in part by News Diggers, gave the meteorology behind the plan. The season is developing under El Niño conditions reinforced by a positive Indian Ocean Dipole, which, in his words, "tilt the odds firmly towards a drier and hotter than normal season". The national seasonal forecast launched on 11 September divides the country into three belts. The southern belt of Southern and Western provinces is the area of greatest concern, with below-normal rainfall and a delayed onset expected; the minister named Sinazongwe, Gwembe, Siavonga, Choma, Kazungula, Livingstone, Senanga, Shang'ombo, Sesheke and Kalabo as the districts likely to be driest. A central transition zone covering Copperbelt, Central and Eastern provinces faces variable rain and a higher risk of prolonged dry spells, while the northern belt — Northern, Muchinga, Luapula and North-Western — can expect normal to above-normal rainfall. Flash floods remain possible in the Barotse Plains and in built-up areas such as Lusaka, and temperatures are expected to be above normal almost everywhere.

Siame also announced a US$3.6 million grant from the Systematic Observation Financing Facility to bring Zambia's automatic weather and rainfall stations up to World Meteorological Organization standards, a World Bank-financed national lightning-detection network, and a digital climate advisory service in Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga and English intended to reach more than one million farmers this season and four million by 2029. Cabinet has approved a National Policy on Meteorology, and a Meteorological Services Bill creating a Zambia Meteorological Authority and a Weather and Climate Fund is to be tabled by the end of the year. News Diggers quotes him telling the House that "in Zambia, rainfall is more than weather".

body.text: What happens to the power supply

body: The question many will ask after the 2023/24 drought, whose lessons the Vice-President invoked, is whether the dams will hold. In Vice-President's Question Time on the same day, reported by the Zambia Daily Mail, Nalumango said Zambia has enough electricity to avoid a return to load-shedding and attributed isolated outages in some areas to routine maintenance. That assurance sits alongside a decision taken earlier this month: Zambia Monitor reported on 15 October that the Zambezi River Authority has cut the 2027 water allocation for power generation at Kariba from 36 billion cubic metres this year to 23 billion, split equally between ZESCO and Zimbabwe Power Company, and projected that usable water in the lake would fall to 5.83 billion cubic metres, about 9 per cent of live storage, by the end of 2027. The authority noted that the lake stood at 480.65 metres on 14 October, up from 477.34 metres a year earlier.

body.title: The numbers in Friday's statements
items: **1.25 million** people, 7 per cent of the population analysed, at risk of acute food insecurity, August 2026 to March 2027
**93** districts affected; relief already sent to prioritised districts in **nine** provinces
**K31.7 million** disbursed so far through the Disaster Risk Management Division
**US$3.6 million** SOFF grant for weather and rainfall stations
**Ten** districts named as likely driest, all in Southern and Western provinces
**23 billion cubic metres** — Kariba's 2027 generation allocation, down from 36 billion (ZRA, 15 October)

body: Nalumango told MPs that disaster-management clusters bringing in line ministries, UN agencies, cooperating partners, churches and civil society have been activated and have produced a 2026/27 El Niño Preparedness and Response Plan covering drought and floods, disease control in people and animals, safe water and sanitation, and the use of strategic grain reserves and market measures to keep staple food available. The Division and its partners are finalising a plan for additional relief food or cash through the lean period. She asked MPs to share the forecast in their constituencies, to encourage farmers to follow advice from the Zambia Meteorological Department and extension officers, and to support the Meteorological Services Bill when it comes to the House.

body.confirmed: That the Vice-President and the Minister of Green Economy delivered ministerial statements on Friday 23 October (Zambia Monitor, News Diggers); the 1.25 million, 93-district and K31.7 million figures and the nine provinces (Zambia Monitor); the three-belt forecast, the ten named districts and the US$3.6 million grant (Zambia Monitor); the Vice-President's statement that there will be no load-shedding (Zambia Daily Mail); the ZRA's 2027 Kariba allocation of 23 billion cubic metres (Zambia Monitor, 15 October).
body.unverified: How large the additional relief package for the lean season will be and when it will be distributed — neither statement, as reported, gave a figure or a date. Whether the no-load-shedding assurance extends into the 2027 dry season, when the reduced Kariba allocation bites, was not addressed in the reports. The forecast is probabilistic: the minister spoke of odds, not certainties.

stories.title: ‘We do not break. We come together’: Hichilema’s message for Zambia at 62 — and the opposition’s answer that there is nothing yet to celebrate
stories.excerpt: Zambia marked 62 years of independence on Saturday 24 October under the theme ‘Our journey, our growth, our future’. In a message issued on the eve of the day, President Hakainde Hichilema paid tribute to the founding generation and set out his Grow Zambia Agenda; Tonse Alliance chairman Sakwiba Sikota told News Diggers he would ‘sadly’ commemorate rather than celebrate, and spoke of a ‘second independence’.

image.label: Zambia at 62
image.caption: The 62nd anniversary of independence fell on Saturday 24 October 2026.

body: Sixty-two years after the flag went up on 24 October 1964, Zambia's Independence Day produced two readings of what freedom now means. The first came from State House on Friday 23 October, in a message from President Hakainde Hichilema reported by Lusaka Times and News Diggers. The second came the same day from Sakwiba Sikota, chairman of the opposition Tonse Alliance, in an interview with News Diggers.

The President's message, under the official theme "Zambia at 62: Our journey, our growth, our future", opened with the founding generation. Lusaka Times reports that he named Kenneth Kaunda, Harry Mwaanga Nkumbula, Simon Mwansa Kapwepwe, Alexander Grey Zulu, Humphrey Mulemba, Nalumino Mundia, Julia Chikamoneka and Betty Chilombo Chilunga among those whose sacrifice the day honours. "Tomorrow marks 62 years since our forefathers and mothers lifted our national flag, with pride and determination," he said, in words carried by both outlets. News Diggers adds that he asked Zambians to mark the day with joy but also with responsibility.

The forward-looking part of the message was economic. According to Lusaka Times, the President said the Grow Zambia Agenda is meant to move the country from stabilisation to accelerated growth, and he listed the targets in plain terms: more maize, more wheat and more copper, more electricity, more tourists and more exports. "We want to produce more maize, more wheat and more copper," he said. He cited progress in schools, hospitals, roads, airports and power stations, praised farmers, miners, young people, women, entrepreneurs and the armed forces, and asked citizens to use the country's natural resources sustainably. The line most likely to be remembered was about resilience: "When we face challenges, we do not break. We come together."

Lusaka Times also used the anniversary to recall Zambia's place in the regional liberation struggle: its hosting of the African National Congress in exile, of ZAPU and ZANU and of SWAPO, and the Rhodesian raids of October 1978 on camps at Chikumbi and Mkushi and of April 1979 on Joshua Nkomo's Lusaka home.

Sikota's reading was different. News Diggers reports that the Tonse Alliance chairman said he would "sadly" commemorate rather than celebrate the anniversary, that in his view freedom no longer exists in Zambia, and that the opposition's focus is now on what he called a "second independence" to reclaim it. He pointed in particular to freedom of expression, saying that the only comment many bloggers now feel able to make on governance is "I don't have a lawyer". The portion of the interview available to non-subscribers ends there, and the Government's response to his remarks, if any, had not been reported by the outlets read for this edition.

The two statements frame the political season ahead. The President's message speaks to a Government asking to be judged on growth; the opposition's speaks to a case that the rule of law and civic space have narrowed, an argument Lusaka Brief reported on Friday in its coverage of the World Justice Project's 2026 Rule of Law Index. Readers can weigh both: the targets in the Grow Zambia Agenda are measurable, and so is the state of the law on speech.

body.title: Independence Day 2026
items: **Theme:** Zambia at 62: Our journey, our growth, our future
**Date:** Saturday 24 October 2026; the President's message was issued on Friday 23 October
**Named founders:** Kaunda, Nkumbula, Kapwepwe, Grey Zulu, Mulemba, Mundia, Chikamoneka and Chilunga (Lusaka Times)
**Opposition line:** a ‘second independence’ — Sakwiba Sikota, Tonse Alliance chairman, to News Diggers

stories.title: Three security zones for one constituency: the police lay out their plan for the Mandevu by-election on 5 November after the Tonse Alliance says its candidate was attacked
stories.excerpt: Inspector General of Police Graphael Musamba said on Saturday 24 October that Mandevu has been divided into three security zones with extra officers drawn from Lusaka Province, and that an alleged assault on Thursday 22 October will be investigated. The Tonse Alliance says FDD candidate Daniel Chisenga and other members were attacked by people in UPND regalia in Raphael Chota ward; the UPND had earlier challenged the alliance to name those it accuses.

image.label: Mandevu, 5 November
image.caption: The Mandevu parliamentary by-election is set for 5 November; police say they have divided the constituency into three security zones.

body: With eleven days to go before Mandevu votes for a new member of Parliament, the police have published their plan for keeping the campaign peaceful, and the opposition has lodged its first formal complaint of violence. Zambia Monitor reports that Inspector General of Police Graphael Musamba, in a statement issued in Lusaka on Saturday 24 October, said the Zambia Police Service "will not tolerate political violence, unlawful assemblies" or any conduct that threatens public peace, and that offenders would face firm and impartial action regardless of party or status.

The plan, as Zambia Monitor describes it, divides the constituency into three security zones, each with its own commander and officers for patrols and rapid response, with additional personnel drawn from across Lusaka Province. Measures are in place to manage campaign movements and polling-day activity. "All parties must respect the campaign timetable agreed upon under the Electoral Commission of Zambia," Musamba said, and he asked parties to avoid inflammatory language, hate speech, tribal remarks and the transporting of cadres to intimidate opponents. He appealed to churches, civil society and the media to work with the police and the Commission, and to residents to vote in large numbers and report suspicious activity. The by-election is on Thursday 5 November.

body.text: The allegation from Raphael Chota ward

body: The statement followed an incident on Thursday 22 October that Musamba said would be investigated. News Diggers reported on Friday that the Tonse Alliance's acting secretary general, Muhabi Lungu, had accused UPND cadres of disrupting the alliance's campaign and attacking its members in Mandevu. According to Lungu's statement as reported, the alliance's candidate Daniel Chisenga — standing on the FDD ticket with the backing of the Tonse Pamodzi alliance — and other members were set upon by people wearing UPND regalia while campaigning in Raphael Chota ward, and one woman was abducted. Lungu called the incident unfortunate and said the alliance had called for a peaceful campaign. News Diggers' second report, on Saturday, quoted Musamba as saying the police are "fully prepared to maintain law and order before, during and after the Mandevu by-election" and will investigate all cases of violence in the constituency, including the alleged attack on Chisenga.

The UPND's position on the campaign was set out before this incident. News Diggers reported on 17 October that the party's deputy secretary general, Getrude Imenda, had challenged the Tonse Alliance to name the people it claimed were threatening Chisenga, said the party was not aware of any such threats, and suggested that an opposition that felt "weak" should withdraw rather than use the UPND's name. No UPND response to the specific allegation of 22 October had been reported by the outlets read for this edition, and Zambia Monitor's report of the police statement does not identify the party of the alleged attackers.

Both the police plan and the complaints will be read as a test of how campaigning is policed in the new Parliament's first months. The questions that remain open are factual ones: whether the police investigation into the Raphael Chota incident produces arrests, whether the abduction reported by the alliance is confirmed, and whether the three-zone plan is visible on the ground when polling opens on 5 November.

body.confirmed: The police statement of 24 October, the three-zone plan, the appeal to parties and the undertaking to investigate the 22 October incident (Zambia Monitor, News Diggers); the by-election date of 5 November (Zambia Monitor); the Tonse Alliance's allegation and the naming of its candidate as Daniel Chisenga (News Diggers); the UPND's earlier challenge to the alliance (News Diggers, 17 October).
body.unverified: Who carried out the alleged attack: the allegation that the attackers were UPND cadres is the alliance's and has not been confirmed by the police, who have said only that the case will be investigated. The reported abduction of a woman is likewise the alliance's account. No arrests had been reported.

stories.title: ‘How do you ask “how did they apprehend?”’: the Vice-President tells MPs the Government will not explain Jay Jay Banda’s capture — and says the lean Cabinet is working
stories.excerpt: In Vice-President's Question Time on Friday 23 October, Mutale Nalumango said the Government would not account for the circumstances in which former Petauke Central MP Emmanuel Jay Banda was brought back from Mozambique and that Banda should explain himself. The Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers report the exchange, which also covered FRA payments, COMESA and the size of the Cabinet.

image.label: Question Time
image.caption: The Vice-President's Friday session in the National Assembly ranged from the Jay Jay Banda case to maize payments and the Cabinet.

body: The Government's position on the capture of Emmanuel Jay Banda hardened a little on Friday 23 October. Asked in Vice-President's Question Time by Sesheke East MP Romeo Kang'ombe whether it was right for some civil society organisations to question how a "criminal" had been brought to face the law, Vice-President Mutale Nalumango said the Government would not explain the circumstances of the former Petauke Central MP's apprehension, and that Banda himself should say how he came to be caught. Both the Zambia Daily Mail and News Diggers report the exchange.

News Diggers quotes her directly: "I think the former minister of home affairs did explain this matter, and it's very important," and then, "How do you ask 'how did they apprehend?'" The paper's account says she questioned how a man who styles himself "Miracle" and claims to foresee events had failed to foresee his own arrest, and that civil society groups should direct their questions to Banda rather than to the Government. The Daily Mail adds that she called for objective commentary, urged citizens to obey the law, warned that anyone involved in criminal activity would face the consequences, and advised law-enforcement agencies to grant bond to accused persons in line with the law and the circumstances of each case.

The question of how Banda was moved from Mozambique to Zambia has been contested since his capture, which News Diggers reported on 16 October. Lusaka Brief reported on 21 October that State House had rejected the civil-society groups' call for an explanation. The Daily Mail reported on Friday that other voices had joined in: Fabian Mutale, described as a democracy advocate, told Crown TV's Spotlight programme that some organisations were questioning the apprehension without addressing Banda's alleged escape from lawful custody, and said Banda should be charged with that as a further offence; the UPND's national youth chairperson, Gilbert Liswaniso, said CSOs should "remain truthful and objective when commenting on national issues" and apply the same standards "regardless of the individuals concerned". The Daily Mail's report does not name or quote the organisations it describes, and their response to Friday's remarks had not been reported by the outlets read for this edition. Banda has not been convicted of any offence arising from these events, and his own account of his return had not been published in those reports.

body.text: Maize money, COMESA and the Cabinet

body: The same session touched three other subjects, according to the Daily Mail. Nalumango told farmers who delivered grain to the Food Reserve Agency that their outstanding payments would be settled soon, pointing to the K14.7 billion set aside in the supplementary budget that Finance Minister Situmbeko Musokotwane presented on Thursday and which Parliament has yet to approve. She said President Hichilema's election as vice-chairperson of COMESA would strengthen the bloc and help Zambia find export markets — "This man is a visionary man," she said. And she told MPs that the lean Cabinet of the second term was working effectively and would not hold up the 2027 budget, a question that has been asked since the President re-appointed his advisers on Thursday with the full Cabinet still awaited. She also, as reported in today's lead, said there would be no return to load-shedding.

body.confirmed: That the Vice-President answered Kang'ombe's question on Friday 23 October and said the Government would not explain Banda's apprehension (Zambia Daily Mail, News Diggers); her quoted words (News Diggers); the remarks of Fabian Mutale and Gilbert Liswaniso (Zambia Daily Mail, 23 October); her statements on FRA payments, COMESA and the Cabinet (Zambia Daily Mail).
body.unverified: The circumstances of Banda's apprehension and transfer from Mozambique, which the Government declines to describe. The allegation that he escaped from lawful custody is an allegation reported by the Daily Mail's interviewees and has not been tested in court. Banda's account has not been reported.

stories.title: US$122 million for Kalulushi: the ZDA signs a protection agreement with Rongxing to double a cathode plant, as the Mines PS says existing mines cannot deliver three million tonnes
stories.excerpt: The Zambia Development Agency signed an investment promotion and protection agreement on Thursday 22 October with Rongxing Investment, a Chinese-owned processor in Kalulushi that plans to lift copper-cathode capacity from 5,500 to 10,000 tonnes a year and add 194 jobs to its 506. At the Mining Insaka the same day, Permanent Secretary Hapenga Kabeta said the three-million-tonne target by 2031 depends on new projects, not expansion of what exists.

image.label: Rongxing, Kalulushi
image.caption: The agreement covers US$122 million of investment, past and planned, in copper processing on the Mufulira road in Kalulushi.

body: The week's mining paperwork ended with a signature. The Zambia Development Agency and Rongxing Investment Limited signed an investment promotion and protection agreement worth US$122 million, the Zambia Daily Mail and the Times of Zambia reported on Friday 23 October. The Daily Mail dates the signing to Thursday 22 October.

Rongxing, which the Daily Mail describes as a subsidiary of Jinxun and the Times of Zambia as owned by Jinxun Resources Company and Shanghai Jinxun New Energy Company Limited, has operated in the Sabina area on the Mufulira road in Kalulushi for a decade, processing copper ore into cathodes and concentrates. The US$122 million is a total of past and future spending: US$42 million already invested in its first two plants since 2016, US$30 million now going into a third plant, and more than US$50 million earmarked for acquiring mining assets and developing resources. The expansion uses solvent extraction–electrowinning and hydrometallurgical processes and is intended to lift cathode output from 5,500 to 10,000 tonnes a year. The company employs 506 people and expects the expansion to add 194 direct jobs, taking the workforce to 700.

body.text: Today's signing demonstrates Zambia's steadfast commitment to supporting private investment.
body.attribution: Albert Halwampa, Director General of the Zambia Development Agency, at the signing ceremony, as reported by the Zambia Daily Mail

body: The Times of Zambia quotes the chairperson of Jinxun Resources, Yuan Rong, describing the agreement as a sign of the company's confidence in Zambia and saying it had "integrated local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) into our supply chains" and intends to build an integrated value chain "from mine to smelter" inside the country. Halwampa, for his part, urged the company to look at the electric-vehicle battery industry and said Zambia should position itself as a manufacturing hub for vehicles, batteries and components.

The agreement was signed in the same week as the Zambia Mining and Investment Insaka in Lusaka, where the Government's three-million-tonnes-a-year copper target by 2031 was examined from several angles. News Diggers reports that on Thursday 22 October the Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Mines and Minerals Development, Dr Hapenga Kabeta, told delegates that expanding production at existing mines would not, on its own, get the country there: substantial growth must come from new projects, including greenfield developments, and exploration should be treated as the foundation on which future output depends. He said the national geophysical survey is 97 per cent complete and should be finished by December. The ZDA's IPPA, which protects an investor's position against changes in the rules, is one of the instruments the Government uses to attract that new money; it does not by itself add a tonne of production.

stories.title: Out of Chimbokaila and back to court: Nakacinda’s ECZ summons trial is put off to 25 November after his lawyer says he is too ill, and the magistrate calls it the last adjournment
stories.excerpt: Raphael Nakacinda was due to open his defence on Friday 23 October to a charge of failing to comply with an Electoral Commission of Zambia summons in November 2022. His lawyer Nkula Bota told Magistrate Mbuywana Sinvula that he was unwell and needed medical attention, the Zambian Observer and News Diggers report; the case resumes on 25 November with a warning that no further adjournments will be granted.

image.label: The summons case
image.caption: The former PF secretary general's trial over an ECZ summons was adjourned to 25 November on grounds of illness.

body: Raphael Nakacinda's first court date since leaving prison lasted only as long as it took to ask for another one. The former Patriotic Front secretary general appeared before Lusaka Magistrate Mbuywana Sinvula on Friday 23 October to begin his defence to a single count of failing to comply with a lawful summons issued by the Electoral Commission of Zambia. According to the Zambian Observer, his lawyer, Nkula Bota, told the court that his client was unwell and needed medical attention; News Diggers reports the submission as being that he was incapable of standing trial because of illness.

The magistrate adjourned the matter to 25 November 2026 and, the Observer reports, warned that no further adjournments would be granted when the case resumes. Both outlets note that this was Nakacinda's first appearance since his release from Chimbokaila earlier in the week after serving a sentence for defaming President Hakainde Hichilema, which Lusaka Brief reported on 22 October.

The case goes back to the by-elections of November 2022. Zambia Monitor reported in August that Nakacinda had alleged the UPND was moving vehicles carrying pre-marked ballot papers to districts holding by-elections; the Observer names the districts as Lusangazi, Mkushi and Mwense. The Commission summoned him over the allegation, and the charge, as News Diggers puts it, is that he failed to comply with that summons between 4 and 7 November 2022. Zambia Monitor reported on 11 August that Magistrate Sinvula had found he had a case to answer and that the defence intended to call ten witnesses in addition to Nakacinda's own sworn evidence; the defence had then been set to open on 14 September. Friday's adjournment pushes that opening into late November.

Nakacinda has not yet given his evidence. Failing to comply with a summons is a distinct charge from the allegation that prompted it; the court has made no finding on whether the claim about ballot papers was true or false, and nothing in the reports suggests it is being asked to.

body.confirmed: The adjournment to 25 November and the magistrate's warning (Zambian Observer); the ground of illness (Zambian Observer, News Diggers); the charge of failing to comply with an ECZ summons and its origin in the November 2022 allegation (News Diggers, Zambia Monitor); the earlier case-to-answer ruling and the ten planned defence witnesses (Zambia Monitor, 11 August).
body.unverified: The nature of the illness, which neither report describes. Whether the defence will call all ten witnesses when the case resumes.

stories.title: History from twelve yards: Red Arrows lose 1–0 in Durban, level the tie and beat Kaizer Chiefs 3–2 on penalties to reach a CAF group stage for the first time
stories.excerpt: Bradley Cross's second-half header at Moses Mabhida Stadium on Friday 23 October cancelled out Alassane Diarra's first-leg goal in Ndola and sent the Confederation Cup tie to a shoot-out. Red Arrows won it 3–2, with Lebohang Maboe, Reeve Frosler and Ethan Chislett missing for Chiefs, and go into the 16-club group stage that begins in November — the first time the Zambia Air Force side has got that far.

image.label: Arrows 3–2 on penalties
image.caption: Red Arrows reached the Confederation Cup group stage for the first time by beating Kaizer Chiefs in a Durban shoot-out.

body: Red Arrows went to Durban on Friday 23 October to protect a one-goal lead and came home having made history the hard way. Kaizer Chiefs won the second leg of their CAF Confederation Cup second preliminary round tie 1–0 at Moses Mabhida Stadium, levelling the aggregate at 1–1 after Arrows' 1–0 win in Ndola a week earlier, and the Zambia Air Force side won the penalty shoot-out 3–2 to reach the competition's group stage for the first time, as CAF's own match report, South Africa's FARPost and TimesLIVE and Zambia's News Diggers all record.

For an hour the tie went as Arrows would have planned it. CAF reports that Thulani Mabaso forced a save from the Arrows goalkeeper in the 11th minute, that Pule Mmodi headed wide at the far post and that Wandile Duba broke through but could not finish, while News Diggers notes that Eliya Mandanji had the visitors' best early chance in the 8th minute, saved by Brandon Petersen, with Ackim Mumba troubling the Chiefs defence. Chiefs' head coach Fernando da Cruz had made five changes from the first leg, FARPost reports, including Bruce Bvuma in goal, and had lost Renaldo Leaner to an injury in the final training session.

body.text: Cross heads Chiefs level, and then the shoot-out

body: The goal came from a set piece. Mfundo Vilakazi, introduced shortly before the hour, delivered a free-kick and Bradley Cross rose to head it in — CAF gives the time as the 65th minute, FARPost as the 66th. Chiefs then pressed for the second goal that would have taken them through, with substitutes Mduduzi Shabalala and Ethan Chislett at the heart of their best moments; Shabalala's shot went straight at the goalkeeper and Velebayi, set up by Chislett, lifted his over the bar. Arrows, who brought on Ricky Banda and Norris Kalamba to hold their shape, defended in numbers and looked for the counter.

The shoot-out was decided by Chiefs' misses. TimesLIVE reports that Lebohang Maboe, Reeve Frosler and Chislett all failed to convert, leaving Arrows winners at 3–2. None of the reports read for this edition lists the Zambian takers kick by kick. The result ends Chiefs' continental season at the first hurdle, a year after they reached the group stage, and sends Arrows into the 16-club group phase of the 2026/27 TotalEnergies CAF Confederation Cup, which CAF says begins in November; the draw date had not been published in the reports consulted.

body.text: We are not here to defend, we are here to complete the job.
body.attribution: Kalililo Kakonje, Red Arrows assistant coach, at the pre-match press conference in Durban on the eve of the match, as reported by News Diggers

body: The attacking promise was not quite kept on the night, but the job was completed. Alassane Diarra's goal in Ndola, the first-leg winner, turned out to be enough to take Arrows to penalties, and the goalkeeper's work and three Chiefs misses did the rest. Lusaka Brief's preview of the tie on Friday said a Confederation Cup group place was at stake; it is now in Arrows' hands.

stories.title: Three games, three defeats, no points: Lea Motyka’s early goal gives France a 1–0 win and ends the Copper Princesses’ U-17 Women’s World Cup
stories.excerpt: Zambia's Under-17 women lost their final Group D match to France 1–0 in Morocco on Saturday 24 October, ZamFoot reports, after a 16th-minute goal by Lea Motyka from a Maelys Ane cross. Coach Carol Kanyemba had called the match ‘do or die’; the defeat follows the 5–0 loss to Japan and the 3–2 loss to Venezuela, and France go through to the round of 16.

image.label: France 1–0 Zambia
image.caption: The Copper Princesses leave the U-17 Women's World Cup in Morocco after three group defeats.

body: The Copper Princesses' FIFA U-17 Women's World Cup ended on Saturday 24 October with the narrowest of their three defeats and the same number of points as the other two. France beat Zambia 1–0 in the final round of Group D matches in Morocco, ZamFoot reports, to finish second in the group and go through to a round-of-16 tie against the United States or China; Zambia finish the group without a point.

The goal came after a quarter of an hour. ZamFoot's account has Maelys Ane running down the French left and crossing into the penalty area, where Zambia failed to clear and Lea Motyka finished in the 16th minute. France nearly doubled the lead soon afterwards when Sharlie Yerro was left unmarked in the box from a corner but could not score. In the second half France controlled the game and protected what they had. Ane was named player of the match.

Head coach Carol Kanyemba had set the stakes plainly. In a pre-match interview on Friday reported by News Diggers, she called the match a do-or-die encounter and said she wanted her players to express themselves without fear. "We know they've got their strengths and weaknesses," she said. Zambia's hope, News Diggers noted, was to progress as one of the best third-placed teams, for which a result against France was essential. The result did not come, and the campaign closes with the 5–0 defeat to Japan in the opener, the 3–2 loss to Venezuela in which Zambia led twice before conceding in the 100th minute — reported by Lusaka Brief on Thursday — and Saturday's 1–0.

ZamFoot reports that Kanyemba's side will now regroup and build on the experience of the tournament for future assignments. The margin of the final match — one goal, against a side that went on to top-two in the group — will be the part of the record the coaching staff point to. The tournament itself continues in Morocco; Lusaka Brief has not been able to confirm the final Group D table from the reports available and gives only Zambia's three results here.

**Venezuela 3–2 Zambia** — Zambia led twice; the winner came in the 100th minute
**France 1–0 Zambia** — Motyka 16', Saturday 24 October
**Points: 0** — eliminated; France advance to the round of 16

stories.title: Mpasela sinks the champions: MUZA beat Power Dynamos 1–0 to lead Stream A, Trident score six and ZESCO finally win in week five of the transitional Super League
stories.excerpt: Solomon Mpasela's 50th-minute goal gave FC MUZA a 1–0 win over defending champions Power Dynamos on Saturday 24 October and a three-point lead in Stream A, ZamFoot reports. Trident put six past Makeni All Stars, ZANACO beat Kansanshi 3–0, ZESCO United beat Mutondo Stars 5–0 for their first win of the season and Green Eagles stayed top of Stream B after a goalless draw with Nkwazi.

image.label: Week five
image.caption: FC MUZA lead Stream A after beating the champions; Green Eagles are unbeaten at the top of Stream B.

body: The defending champions were beaten on Independence Day. FC MUZA defeated Power Dynamos 1–0 on Saturday 24 October, Solomon Mpasela scoring in the 50th minute, to move to ten points from four matches and a three-point lead at the top of Stream A of the transitional Super League, according to ZamFoot's round-up of week five. Power stay on six points, four behind MUZA with the same number of games played.

The weekend's other Stream A results were lopsided. Trident beat Makeni All Stars 6–1 at the Sentinel grounds, with Sam Sikasote scoring twice — the first in the 7th minute from a Jericho Mwila free-kick — Boyd Kauya adding one, Gradi Bakodila two in the 63rd and 65th minutes and Kelvin Mwamba the sixth near the end; Simon Tembo's 81st-minute goal was Makeni's reply, and they stay bottom on one point with a goal difference of minus nine. ZANACO beat Kansanshi Dynamos 3–0 through a Kiala Wa Kiala header and two goals from Araina Lambert to go third on seven points, and Nchanga Rangers edged NAPSA Stars 1–0 with a 3rd-minute goal from Mwiza Siwale.

In Stream B, ZESCO United's season finally started. Anthony Shipanuka scored in the first minute at the Trade Fair grounds in Ndola, Kennedy Musonda added two in quick succession either side of the 37th minute, one of them a penalty, Happy Nsiku headed a fourth from a corner on the hour and Elvis Addae completed a 5–0 win over Mutondo Stars late on after a goalkeeping error. ZESCO move to five points and second place; Mutondo remain pointless after four straight defeats. Green Eagles, held 0–0 by Nkwazi, stay top on ten points with three wins, a draw, six goals scored and one conceded, five clear of ZESCO and of Green Buffaloes, who have a game in hand.

The transitional season's format, as ZamFoot describes it, splits the 20 clubs into two streams of ten, each playing 18 matches, with the two stream winners meeting in a final on 31 January 2027. ZESCO have a rescheduled week-three fixture against Roan United to come in midweek.

**Stream B:** ZESCO United 5–0 Mutondo Stars · Green Eagles 0–0 Nkwazi
**Stream A top four:** MUZA 10 (4 games), Nkana 9 (3), ZANACO 7 (4), Konkola Blades 6 (4)
**Stream B:** Green Eagles 10, ZESCO United 5, Green Buffaloes 5 (3 games)

analysis.title: The 2023/24 drought is the yardstick for this El Niño, and the plan shows it
analysis.body: Friday's two statements are best read against the 2023/24 drought, which the Vice-President herself invoked when she asked MPs to have their constituents preserve this year's stocks. This time the warnings have come before the season rather than during it, the needs assessment has put a number on the exposure — 1.25 million people in 93 districts — and some relief money has reached the provinces before the lean months begin. That is the case for saying lessons were learned. The case for caution is in what was not said. K31.7 million is a modest sum against the population named, and neither statement, as reported, gave the size or timing of the main lean-season package of food or cash. The Vice-President's assurance on electricity speaks to the present; the Zambezi River Authority has already cut Kariba's 2027 generation allocation from 36 to 23 billion cubic metres, and a dry season would make that cut bite harder. What to watch: whether the Food Reserve Agency's large maize stock is released into southern markets, whether the Meteorological Services Bill reaches the House before the rains, and the first Zambia Meteorological Department bulletins on when the onset arrives in Southern and Western provinces.

analysis.title: Mandevu is a small by-election carrying a large test
analysis.body: One Lusaka constituency, eleven more days of campaigning and a single seat will not change the balance of the National Assembly. But both sides have already told voters how to read it. The Tonse Alliance's complaint of an attack in Raphael Chota ward, if the police confirm it, would be the first recorded violence of the new term; the UPND's earlier reply — name the attackers or withdraw — sets up a dispute about evidence that the police investigation can settle. The Inspector General's three-zone plan is unusually specific for a by-election, and that is to the police's credit; it also gives observers a checklist. Arguments on each side deserve a hearing: the opposition says intimidation is being used against a campaign already struggling for resources, the ruling party says the allegations are unproven and politically convenient. What is unknown is who the attackers were and whether the abduction reported by the alliance happened as described. What to watch: arrests or their absence before 5 November, and whether the Electoral Commission's campaign timetable is enforced evenly.

analysis.title: What a group stage gives Red Arrows that a cup run never has
analysis.body: Red Arrows have reached a CAF group stage for the first time, and the significance is less the scoreline in Durban than the calendar that follows it. A group stage means a run of fixtures against clubs from across the continent from November into the new year, the income CAF attaches to that phase, and the kind of regular continental football that Zambian clubs have rarely managed to sustain. It also means strain: a transitional domestic season of 18 league matches with a final set for 31 January, and travel budgets that a Zambia Air Force club will have to meet. The assistant coach's promise to attack in Durban was not quite kept — Arrows defended for most of the second half — but the discipline that saw them through a shoot-out is exactly what group football rewards. What is unknown is the draw, the opponents and where Arrows will host. What to watch: the date CAF sets for the group draw, how Arrows handle a midweek-and-weekend rhythm, and whether the domestic fixture list makes room for them.
